title: Lab 11 — Quiz 1
subtitle: Unknown ID Part 2 — catalase, coagulase, MSA, hemolysis

questions.prompt: Hydrogen peroxide was added to this sample and bubbles formed. What is the result?
questions.explanation: Catalase breaks down H2O2: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2. The O2 bubbles = positive.

why.A: Negative = no bubbles after adding H2O2.
why.C: Coagulase is read as clumping, not bubbles.

questions.prompt: Hydrogen peroxide was added to this sample and NO bubbles formed. What is the result?
questions.explanation: No bubbles = no catalase enzyme = catalase negative.

why.D: The catalase test is rapid and needs no incubation.

questions.prompt: The catalase test is a quick way to differentiate:

options.text: S. aureus from other Staphylococcus species

questions.explanation: Catalase: Staphylococcus (+) vs Streptococcus (−). A rapid test with no incubation needed.

questions.prompt: In this coagulase tube test, the top tube shows clumping. What is the result?

options.text: Coagulase negative — consistent with S. epidermidis
Coagulase positive — consistent with S. aureus

questions.explanation: Coagulase converts fibrinogen into fibrin (clumping). Most S. aureus strains are coagulase positive.

why.D: Hemolysis is read on blood agar.

questions.prompt: Why is coagulase considered a virulence factor?

options.text: Coagulase+ bacteria coat themselves in fibrin, protecting them from phagocytosis
It breaks down hydrogen peroxide made by immune cells
It lyses red blood cells to release iron
It ferments mannitol to produce acid

questions.explanation: Coagulase converts fibrinogen to fibrin; coating the surface in fibrin protects the pathogen from phagocytosis.

why.D: Mannitol fermentation is read on MSA.

questions.prompt: Read this MSA plate (S. aureus): growth and yellow medium. What is the result?
questions.explanation: MSA: growth = salt-tolerant; yellow = mannitol fermented to acid (phenol red turns yellow).

why.C: There is growth, so it is salt-tolerant.

questions.prompt: Read this MSA plate (S. epidermidis): growth, but the medium stays red/pink. What is the result?
questions.explanation: Growth with red-orange medium = salt-tolerant but doesn't ferment mannitol.

questions.prompt: This MSA plate (E. coli) shows no growth. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: No growth on MSA = not salt-tolerant.

why.D: MSA tests salt tolerance, not Gram reaction.

questions.prompt: What are the differential components of mannitol salt agar?
questions.explanation: MSA is selective for salt-tolerant (halophilic) bacteria and differential with mannitol + phenol red.

why.A: The high salt is the selective component.

questions.prompt: Read this blood agar plate: clear zones of complete red blood cell lysis around colonies. What type of hemolysis is this?
questions.explanation: Beta = complete lysis of RBCs. On the key, S. pyogenes is beta-hemolytic.

why.C: Only alpha, beta and gamma are covered.

questions.prompt: Read this blood agar plate: partial lysis of red blood cells (greenish, darkened agar). What type of hemolysis is this?
questions.explanation: Alpha = partial lysis of RBCs. On the key, S. pneumoniae is alpha-hemolytic.

why.C: There is growth on this plate.

questions.prompt: Read this blood agar plate: colonies grow but the red agar around them is unchanged. What type of hemolysis is this?
questions.explanation: Gamma = no lysis of red blood cells.
Blood agar (sheep's blood): enriched for fastidious growth; differential for hemolysis. Useful for differentiating Streptococcus spp.

why.A: MSA and MacConkey are selective + differential.
why.D: Blood is a special added ingredient (enriched).

questions.prompt: Which pH indicator is found in mannitol salt agar, and what color is a positive result?
questions.explanation: Phenol red (MSA, TSI, fermentation broths): yellow = acid from fermentation (positive).

why.B: Bromothymol blue is in citrate agar.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the coagulase test is FALSE?

options.text: Most S. aureus strains are coagulase positive
It is a rapid test that needs no incubation

questions.explanation: The CATALASE test differentiates Staphylococcus from Streptococcus. Coagulase differentiates S. aureus from other Staphylococcus spp.

why.E: True — as stated on the slide.
